chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ṣafwān and Faḍālah, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:

I asked him about ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah. He said: “You begin with your two hands, then wash your private part, then pour over your head three times, then pour over the rest of your body two times; so whatever the water has flowed over, it has purified.”

key_terms.بِكَفَّيْكَ: with your two hands; indicating the first part to wash
key_terms.رَأْسِكَ: your head, over which water is poured three times
key_terms.سَائِرِ جَسَدِكَ: the remainder of your body after the head
key_terms.طَهَّرَهُ: purified it; meaning the water renders the reached area ritually pure
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after the state of janabah
key_terms.فَرْجَكَ: your private part, to be washed before the rest of the bath

ai.seo_question: How is ghusl al-janabah performed according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the method of performing ghusl for janabah in an orderly sequence. It outlines washing the hands, then the private part, then pouring water over the head three times and over the rest of the body twice, emphasizing that whatever water reaches is thereby purified.
